title: Microsoft Teams: users can report a security concern in meetings
summary: The briefing is supported by the roadmap, the supplied Microsoft notice and Microsoft Learn. The default-on state, inclusion in Defender for Office 365 Plan 1 and Plan 2, and documented controls check out; the page explicitly identifies the remaining documentation gaps. All eight Learn pages flagged by the pre-check were accessible during this review.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Reporting an item to Microsoft copies associated meeting and participant metadata.
claims.quote: When a user reports a Teams item to Microsoft, the following data associated with the item is copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable:

claims.claim: Meeting and participant metadata submitted to Microsoft is included in ongoing algorithm reviews.
claims.quote:
copied and included in ongoing algorithm reviews, as applicable:

    - Message content.
    - Headers.
    - Attachments.
    - Routing metadata.
    - Call metadata and any other related information.
    - Meeting metadata.
    - Meeting participant metadata.

claims.claim: Microsoft personnel might review submitted meeting and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items.
claims.quote: Microsoft personnel might read submitted messages and files and review submitted call, meeting, and participant metadata, which is typically not permitted for Teams items in Microsoft 365.

claims.claim: Submitted content is stored in data centres in the USA.
claims.quote: Submitted content is stored in secured, compliance-audited data centers located in the USA and is deleted as soon as it's no longer required.

claims.claim: Microsoft cites Microsoft and my reporting mailbox as the default destination.
claims.quote: That's why we use **Send the reported items to** > **Microsoft and my reporting mailbox** as the default.

claims.quote: If you select **Send the reported items to** > **My reporting mailbox only**, reported items don't go to Microsoft for analysis unless an admin manually submits the item from the **User reported** tab

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration -Identity Global -ReportMeeting Enabled|Disabled controls the meeting reporting options through MicrosoftTeams PowerShell.
claims.quote: Controls whether end users can access the "Report a concern" and "Report as not a concern" options in the meeting experience (including meeting UI and meeting chat).

claims.claim: The ReportMeeting configuration is tenant-wide.
claims.quote: Use this cmdlet to set the configuration for your organization. ... The only valid input is Global

claims.claim: Learn does not explicitly identify ReportMeeting as the backing parameter for the Allow users to report meetings UI policy.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow users to report meetings" "ReportMeeting". Opened end-user-reporting-teams-meeting, submissions-teams and Set-CsTeamsMeetingConfiguration; both surfaces are documented, but no explicit UI-to-parameter mapping was found.

claims.quote: go to **Settings** > **Email & collaboration** > **Teams user reported settings** tab. ... go to the **Microsoft Teams** section for the **Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams** setting.

claims.claim: The Defender monitoring setting is meaningful only if the corresponding Teams reporting experience is enabled.
claims.quote: When the applicable setting is turned off, users can't report those items within Teams, so the corresponding setting in the Microsoft Defender portal is irrelevant.

claims.claim: The documented Exchange Online PowerShell call with ReportChatMessageEnabled true, ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled true and ReportChatMessageAddresses sends reports to Microsoft and the specified mailbox.
claims.quote:
#### Send reported Teams items to Microsoft and the reporting mailbox
Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy -Identity DefaultReportSubmissionPolicy -ReportChatMessageEnabled $true -ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $true -ReportChatMessageAddresses "securityadmin@contoso.com"

claims.claim: The documented Microsoft-only command uses ReportChatMessageEnabled true, ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled false and EnableUserEmailNotification true.
claims.quote: The value `-ReportChatMessageEnabled $true` is required to achieve **Send reported items to** > **Microsoft only**. The values `-EnableUserEmailNotification $true` and `-ReportChatMessageToCustomizedAddressEnabled $false` are also required.

claims.quote:
go to **Analytics & reports** > **Protection reports**.

claims.claim: The Teams report documentation lists Calling, Chats and channels, and User categories, but does not document a meetings category.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "API" and "User reported security submissions" "license". Opened end-user-reported-security-signal; its overview and report-category steps list Calling, Chats and channels, and User, with no meetings category.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the Defender Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams setting was established.
claims.quote: Searched: "Monitor reported items in Microsoft Teams" PowerShell Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy. Opened submissions-teams and searched Set-ReportSubmissionPolicy for monitoring; its Teams parameters document destinations, not this monitoring toggle.

claims.claim: No documented command or API for reviewing user-reported meeting submissions in Defender was established.
claims.quote: Searched: "meeting" "User reported" "PowerShell" submissions; "meeting" "threatSubmission". Opened the SecOps guide and Graph beta threatSubmission reference; the latter covers email, attachment and URL submissions, not meeting reports.

claims.claim: No supported command for changing the built-in reported-call alert policies used by meeting reports was established.
claims.quote: Searched: built in alert policies Set-ProtectionAlert Teams call reported user security risk edit PowerShell. Read alert-policies and the Set-ProtectionAlert search excerpt, which says that cmdlet cannot edit default alert policies; no applicable alternative found.

claims.claim: No documented automation equivalent for the Teams admin center user-reported security submissions report was established.
claims.quote: Searched: "User reported security submissions" "API"; Teams user reported meeting submissions Graph API protection reports PowerShell. Opened end-user-reported-security-signal; it documents UI viewing and CSV export, not an API or cmdlet.

claims.claim: No Graph endpoint for meeting security reports was found in Learn.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams user reported meeting submissions Graph API protection reports PowerShell; "meeting" "threatSubmission". Opened Graph beta security-threatSubmission; documented types are emailThreatSubmission, fileThreatSubmission and urlThreatSubmission, not meeting reports.

claims.claim: The messaging policies page documents Report a security concern for messages, without confirming that it governs meetings.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams meeting report security concern end-user-reporting-teams-meeting submissions-teams ReportMeeting; "Allow users to report meetings" "ReportMeeting". Opened messaging-policies-in-teams and submissions-teams; meeting reporting is documented separately.

claims.claim: The meeting reporting page does not give a fully named navigation path to Allow users to report meetings.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow users to report meetings" "ReportMeeting". Opened end-user-reporting-teams-meeting and submissions-teams; the former says to open the policy or settings page controlling meeting reporting without naming that page, and the latter links to it.
